historical_significance: Stephen William Hawking (8 January 1942 - 14 March 2018) was a British theoretical physicist and Lucasian Professor of Mathematics at Cambridge (1979-2009). He proved, with Roger Penrose, the Penrose-Hawking singularity theorems showing general relativity predicts spacetime singularities; discovered that black holes emit thermal radiation ('Hawking radiation'), uniting quantum mechanics, general relativity and thermodynamics; proved the area theorem of black holes; and, with James Hartle, proposed the no-boundary wave function of the universe. Diagnosed with motor neurone disease (ALS) at 21 and given two years to live, he worked in a wheelchair for over five decades and became the most influential science communicator of his era — A Brief History of Time sold over 25 million copies.
